notes: Schema: episodes_*.jsonl lines have fields: task (int id, global 0-14 across the suite, 5 tasks per level L0/L1/L2), ep (episode index; initial state is deterministic via init_states[ep % len(init_states)] at vlm_pipeline/run_guided_libero_safety_eval.py:1365, so equal (suite,level,task,ep) => identical initial state), success (bool), violation (bool, EPISODE-level only - no per-timestep/per-object violation record is logged; 'violated_hazard_guess' = the episode's active guard list, i.e. the object(s) the violation was measured against; re-render the episode to localize the contact frame), steps, hazards, guard, movers, ident_correct, eef_path_len. task_language taken from sibling results_*.json per_task. Board arms per frozen FINAL BOARD (results_tables/fgd_tier_gt_results.md, 2026-08-09 batch-key-collision correction): base = ls_ours_parity_full/base_par (exec-parity, guidance=false) + ls_nboost/base_oa_n20 restricted to ep<=9 (n-boost reuses ep indices => same init states; ep>=10 has no ours counterpart and its init identity is unverified); ours-noGT = ls_ours_parity_full/nogt_par_full (oa cell 68.7/0.7) and ls_cone_confirm/F3_oah_nogt_cone (oah cell 58.9/1.7). Caveats: (1) hs and aff have 0 base violations -> no pairs possible; (2) policy sampling is stochastic, so identical init does not imply identical trajectory - which is the point of the paired teaser; (3) oa L2 t11 base violations are succeed-but-violate (task completed while clipping the shampoo bottle) - the strongest teaser story: base finishes the task unsafely, ours finishes it safely; (4) violation_replicates_in marks pairs whose base violation reproduced in the independent n-boost batch at the same (task,ep) - most robust picks.
